Phil Carstairs and Steve Fowler, who had only decided to race a few minutes before the "off" due to sore tendons, had both made up several places but the veteran Ulliot, last scorer for the south coast club, was going like a train and was now just about to go into the 30s.
Roger came back again to enter the funnel 10th and thus claim an Inter-Counties slot and veteran Steve Fowler proved yet again what tough guy he is, shoring up the team in 28th.

A couple of our guys were starting to look uncomfortable but Steve Fowler was losing positions by the score. A suspect ankle had really gone nasty on him and as he dropped back in great pain, now our tenth man, he was was just praying that another Belgravian would come past and allow him to pull out.

Steve Fowler always produces the goods when he turns out and Phil Carstairs was another to turn in a strong run. Our Junior Captain Kevin Quinn reached his best ever league position and scanning through the results we note that no other under 20 appeared ahead of him.
There was more fine sprinting from Ladejo and Marlon Dickson but once again two veterans got on the scoring sheet in a big way as Jim Estall and Steve Fowler took both first places in the 5k.

Throw in a couple of runners who missed their proper start times – Steve Fowler went off at about 14:25 instead of 14:00 while James Skilbeck-Nelson set out much later than he should have done – and poor Jacqui Smiter's asthma attack in mid-race, and one can see that there was as much drama in the event as ever.
